newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-BAe Australia says sees 1997 sales rise.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-BAe Australia says sees 1997 sales rise.

text.p: British Aerospace Plc's (BAe) Australian unit said on Tuesday it expected calendar 1997 sales to rise, underpinned by export orders which more than doubled last year.
"We'll be able to achieve modest organic (sales) growth within the company and a lot would be generated by our exports," chief executive Robin Southwell told Reuters.
BAe Australia's 1996 sales totalled about A$275 million including exports of A$110 million, Southwell said.

He said A$50 million of last year's exports included supplies to BAe Australia's British parent, while the balance included infra-red jamming and rocket decoy systems sold to customers in the Middle East and Asia-Pacific regions.

"I've asked the guys to at least as well as last year without that A$50 million so we're looking at a significant increase in exports in our own right and I'm confident we can achieve that," Southwell said.
Exports represented about 40 percent of BAe Australia's total revenues, Southwell said.
Southwell said the company would soon announce a major export order for the Australian-made Foxhound armoured vehicle.
When asked if the customer was from the Middle East, Southwell replied: "Could be." He declined to give further details.
A company source said the order was worth about A$20 million and had been placed by a Middle East client.
Southwell said BAe Australia had sold three Jetstream passenger aircraft in February to New Zealand-based Inglis Aircraft Ltd for an undisclosed sum.
"During 1996 we placed 17 aircraft in the Australasian market. These transactions were valued at US$70 million.
"Of that 17, eight of them were BAe 146 regional jets," he added.
